title: Four Legends, One Night: Inside Wawrinka's Farewell in Geneva

 Wawrinka’s Farewell Unites Federer, Murray and Monfils 
 ATP Tour Wawrinka’s Farewell Unites Federer, Murray and Monfils 
 Jim Flannigan | 23 October 2026 | 4 min read Stan Wawrinka says goodbye - Photo: IMAGO/PsnewZ Share this article
 Add us as a preferred source on Google 
 Stan Wawrinka will close out his professional tennis career on December 19 in Geneva, and the guest list for his farewell exhibition has confirmed what the sport rarely gets: four genuine legends on the same court at the same time. Roger Federer, Andy Murray and Gaël Monfils will all be present at Palexpo for an evening billed as “One Last Backhand.”
 Monfils back on court despite early exit
 The Monfils inclusion gives the event a particular charge . The Frenchman entered retirement earlier than planned, with the sport’s drug-testing organisation listing him among retired players from October 5. Many had expected him to play events in Lyon and Paris before ending his career, but his competitive career appears to have finished with a second-round defeat to Learner Tien at the 2026 US Open. The abrupt exit left fans short-changed, and the Geneva date gives them a proper goodbye.
 Wawrinka is expecting Monfils to participate in his farewell exhibition on December 19, despite Monfils having ended his own career prematurely due to personal reasons. Monfils remains listed on the official programme, with Wawrinka counting on the Frenchman’s presence for a scheduled one-set singles match, followed by a two-set doubles contest in which Wawrinka and Federer will face Monfils and Murray.
 The format alone is worth the ticket. A singles set between two players who have spent twenty years entertaining crowds in completely different ways, Wawrinka’s blunt, heavyweight ground game against Monfils’s acrobatic improvisation, and then a doubles pairing that reunites the Swiss Davis Cup axis for one final time.
 What Federer and Wawrinka built together
 Wawrinka and Federer won Olympic doubles gold at the 2008 Beijing Games and helped Switzerland capture its first Davis Cup title in 2014. That bond runs deeper than any rivalry. Federer retired in 2022, so Geneva will mark his first competitive appearance on Swiss soil in years, even if the occasion is an exhibition. The home crowd will not be ambivalent about that.
 Murray brings an extensive record to the event. The former world No. 1 won three Grand Slam singles titles, two Olympic singles gold medals and the 2016 ATP Finals, and retired from professional tennis in 2024 after a career that overlapped with Wawrinka’s most successful years.
 The reunion carries particular significance because of the players’ shared history. Wawrinka, Federer, Murray and Monfils were all part of the same generation, the one that came of age in the shadow of the Big Three and still carved out legacies of genuine weight. Three Grand Slam titles each for Wawrinka and Murray. Twenty for Federer. Thirteen ATP titles and two Grand Slam semi-finals for Monfils. One night, four careers.
 What Wawrinka is leaving behind
 The 41-year-old announced that 2026 would be his last season after more than two decades on tour. The farewell exhibition will mark the conclusion of a career that brought him three Grand Slam singles titles, Olympic doubles gold and a Davis Cup triumph with Switzerland. He won those Slams in three different years across three different surfaces, which tells you something about how complete a player he was on his best days.
 Wawrinka spoke about the evening in terms that reflect how long he has been thinking about this moment. “Over all these years, I’ve had the chance to experience so many incredible emotions thanks to tennis, but above all, thanks to you,” he said. “Before I leave, I wanted to organise one last event to thank you and say goodbye.”
 All four men were intrinsically linked during their time on the ATP Tour for much of the 2000s and 2010s. No ranking consequence hangs over December 19. No prize money, no draw implications. Just four players who defined an era, with one of them stepping off the court for good. Wawrinka’s last ATP tournament before the exhibition is the Swiss Indoors in Basel, which begins on October 24.

 Jim Flannigan
